title: Change order mid-project: cumulative catch-up

company.company_business: IT implementation and managed services for mid-size Indian businesses

narrative_template:
On 1 May 2025 {company_name} agreed a fixed-price contract with {customer} to build and roll out a payroll platform for ₹{original_price}. It is one performance obligation satisfied over time, and progress is measured cost-to-cost. The original estimate of total cost was ₹{original_est_cost}.

On 1 November 2025, when costs incurred to date were ₹{costs_at_mod}, the parties signed change order CO-1: {company_short} will add a leave-management module for an extra ₹{change_price}, expected to cost ₹{change_cost}. The module is built into the same platform and shares its data model, so the customer cannot use it on its own. The extra price was negotiated; it is not the module's standalone selling price.

What to produce: (1) the measure of progress immediately after the modification; (2) the cumulative catch-up adjustment to revenue on 1 November 2025 (negative if it reduces revenue); (3) the cumulative revenue on the contract at 1 November 2025 after the adjustment; (4) how CO-1 is accounted for, and why.

Answer rules: state amounts in rupees rounded to the nearest rupee (an answer within 0.5% or ₹1,000 of the key, whichever is larger, counts as correct); state percentages to one decimal place, and use the unrounded percentage when you compute amounts; the financial year runs from 1 April to 31 March. All names are fictional.

rubric.text: Progress after CO-1: costs to date over the new total estimate (original estimate plus the module's cost).
Cumulative catch-up: revenue to date on the modified contract less the revenue recognised before CO-1.
Cumulative revenue after the adjustment: the modified price times the new measure of progress.

Accounts for CO-1 as part of the existing contract (para 21(b)): the transaction price and the measure of progress are both updated, and the effect is recognised as a cumulative catch-up adjustment to revenue on the modification date.

Explains why the module is not distinct from the platform (it is integrated into one combined output and highly interdependent, paras 27 and 29), so CO-1 is neither a separate contract (para 20) nor treated prospectively (para 21(a)).

model_answer_template: CO-1 adds work that is not distinct from the platform already being built, so it is part of the existing contract (para 21(b)); it is not a separate contract (para 20) and not prospective (para 21(a)). The new total estimated cost is the original estimate plus the module's cost, so progress after CO-1 = costs to date / new total = {progress_after_modification}%. Revenue to date = (original price + change price) x new progress = ₹{revenue_to_date_after_modification}. Revenue recognised before CO-1 was original price x costs to date / original estimate, so the cumulative catch-up recognised on 1 November 2025 is ₹{catch_up_adjustment}.
